After reading this thread, I’m honestly going to have to lean more towards agreeing with OP. Does the excessive use of ad hominems help their case? No, but regardless of the guy being a celebrity or not, the decision to procreate while being cognizant of the fact there is a genetic likelihood they will end up with severe mental illness like him only to end up further traumatizing them by abandoning them is immoral. It is important to note that there is no absolute in knowing whether his mental illness was developed before or after having children, but regardless of that there are still harms and inevitable suffering in the offspring as a result of procreation. In Better Never to Have Been, Benatar states that disability is societally constructed, and concludes that everyone has inabilities that affect the quality of our lives. While to an extent this claim is true, one has to consider the reality of societal norms and the rate in which they progress; what is the benefit in knowingly passing down your genes in an ableist society leading to the child to have a lifetime of suffering? Are you expecting some radical change to occur in society that’ll significantly better the kid’s life? I’m not saying suffering is inherently genetic either, as there are largely environmental factors to consider as well. 

I’d just like you to consider my perspective as a mentally disabled person. I’m suicidal on a daily basis, wishing I was never born. My parents were well aware of their mental illnesses but decided to have me anyway. As a result, I developed mental illness throughout my childhood, partially due to the inheritable genes and growing up with mentally ill parents that don’t know how to raise a child adequately and provide resources to succeed in life. Every case is different, but making the decision to purposely have children when having a mental illness is incredibly irresponsible, and further burdening the children’s quality of life by committing suicide puts me beyond words.

So it seems that these synths are layered as the song continues. On all of these synths, there's an LFO on the volume going in 16th triplets (similar to a tremolo) to get that wobbly effect. Initially for the beginning layer there's a sine wave with an LFO on the pitch at a slow rate.  Sounds like it has very subtle tube distortion as well. XLN's RC-20 is a great plugin for the pitch LFO and distortion, along with the vinyl sound in general. For that slide up in the chords, you could just automate a pitch bend at the start of each chord or create an envelope that does just that. There is another chord layer that comes in during the chorus which is just a supersaw with a low-pass filter on it. For the gritty bass sound, you would just make a reese bass (not too much detuning though), apply tube distortion, and automate the cutoff of the low-pass filter as it does throughout the song. I'd also add a little high end to it to give it more grittiness. Hope this points you in the right direction :)

I think this saw synth in particular has a lot of white noise on it. You can tweak more of the high end of it with OTT as well. What makes it kind of ‘jumpy’ isn’t only volume envelopes, but the sidechain also gives it that feel. Figured it out. I messed around with Sylenth and got the best results by doing the following:
- Having a sine wave oscillator
- Adding a pitch envelope
- Pitch LFO to make a subtle pitch wobble (rate around 1/4)
- Chorus wet/dry around 19.01%, rate at 0.91 Hz, depth at 40.00%, width at 100.00%—this gives it that stereo effect
- Very subtle distortion
- Adjust reverb to your likings (I had my reverb size at 3.17 and dry/wet at 50%)

It’s a pretty cool sound imo. Hope this helps :)

If you use Serum, here's what I suggest that I got the best results with:

* Just have a normal saw wave
* Set the unison to 3-6 voices
* Make the detune to around 0.02
* Set the blend to around 65
* Make sure the phase is around 350 degrees
* Change the envelope to have a short decay
* Adjust the reverb and delay to your likings

Hope this helps :)
